proposals.before: Is this not the superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
proposals.after: Surely this is no mere superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
proposals.reason: The rhetorical 豈…哉 denies that ritual-music is a mere ornamental excess of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; the literal rendering as “Is this not…” inverts the denial into an affirmation.

proposals.before: Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when Zhenyou moved south, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.
proposals.after: Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when the court moved south in the Zhenyou period, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.
proposals.reason: The literal English makes Zhenyou the subject of the southward move; 貞祐南遷 means the court relocated south during the Zhenyou era.

proposals.reason: 宣孝 is the crown prince posthumous title Xuanxiao, not two descriptive English epithets.
